compliance_risks.could_misstate: Classifying any product from its name. Doing so produces errors in both directions - calling insurance a membership, and calling a service a discount.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Never type or describe a product from its name. Read the Info page.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: Nothing client-facing. This is an internal rule.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: Product names in this portfolio are unreliable indicators of product type IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. 'AWA SimpleShield Membership Plan' is fixed indemnity insurance. 'Prime Health Pass Discount' is described on its own page as a Diagnostic Services Product delivering services. Between April and September NEO inserted the word 'Membership' into four Safe Guard product names without any evident change of type. Meanwhile 'AssistPro Discount' genuinely is a discount program.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: Before any add-on is described on a call, and before any tooling assigns it a category.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Nothing directly - this is a defect in the document, not in what the agent says. But it means the clause telling the client who to contact about claims may be unreadable, and the client may later say they were never told who their agent was.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not tell a client the agreement names their agent.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: Give the client your own name, agency and email verbally on the recorded call, and confirm you are their contact for benefit and claims questions. Do not rely on the agreement to have done it.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: The FirstEnroll enrollment-agreement template served on the live storefront contains unrendered variables - $parentcompany, $product_label, $agent_fullname, $agent_Email, $parentemail - confirmed on two unrelated product families (American Financial Critical Illness page 38175, and Health Choice Silver page 32339). The affected clauses are the third-party administrator disclaimer, the Plan and Claims Inquiries clause and the Writing Agent Contact block.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: Raise with FirstEnroll whether the executed enrollment document renders these variables. See G-039.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Everything, and STM is the worst place for it. With no schedule published, an agent describing deductibles, coinsurance, term length or what is covered is describing short-term medical from general knowledge. Separately: telling a client to check the First Health directory when the plan may run on PHCS.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not describe how short-term medical 'usually' works. Do not name a network until C-025 is resolved. Do not answer any pre-existing question - short-term medical almost always carries a pre-existing exclusion and no source held states this one.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: Do not quote these plans from the portal. Read AccessHealthBrochure2.pdf first and quote only from it.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: The FirstEnroll Info page for both Access Health short-term medical products contains one line of content - a provider-search link - and nothing else. The TERMS panel is empty. The line labels the network 'First Health Network' while pointing to a MultiPlan PHCS lookup URL.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: AccessHealthBrochure2.pdf is in Drive and unread. See G-050 and C-025.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Three things. First, presenting this as guaranteed-issue - it is not, and a client who answers Yes to a health question is not eligible. Second, quoting the 12-month figure agents may carry over from other products in the book; this one is 36 months. Third, describing the Pre-Existing Waiver Rider as covering pre-existing conditions - it waives conditions covered during a PRIOR COVERAGE PERIOD, carrying continuity between consecutive terms. It does nothing for a condition the client had before the first term.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not say guaranteed acceptance. Do not say twelve months. Do not say the waiver rider covers pre-existing conditions. Do not quote a benefit column until the Plan 1/2/3 mapping is established - see G-053.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: This is short-term medical insurance and it is medically underwritten - there are health questions and you need to answer no to all of them. Pre-existing conditions are not covered, and it looks back three years at anything a doctor advised, diagnosed, treated or prescribed for. Sickness benefits start after five days, cancer after thirty, injuries immediately.

source.sec: held in Drive and linked from FirstEnroll pages 28230 and 28231

compliance_risks.verified_fact: Access Health STM is medically underwritten - eligibility requires the applicant to 'answer No to all the questions in the enrollment application for insurance'. It carries a 36-MONTH pre-existing lookback, the longest in the portfolio, defined to include consultations, diagnostic tests and prescription medicines, and the brochure states in capitals that PRE-EXISTING CONDITIONS ARE NOT COVERED. Waiting periods: 5 days sickness, 30 days cancer, none for injuries. Coverage terminates at age 65 or on becoming effective under Medicare, whichever is first.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: The carrier's legal name is disputed inside the brochure itself - see C-030. Cite Certificate form AF ST CERT 818 rather than naming the insurer.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Blending the insurance and the membership. A client who hears 'you get prescription coverage' when the policy excludes outpatient drugs and the membership offers a discount card has been told something false. The same trap applies to dental, speech therapy and diabetic supplies - each is excluded from the insurance and discounted by the membership.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Never let 'covered' and 'discounted' occupy the same sentence. Do not quote the $1,000,000 coverage period maximum without the condition caps - a client with a knee problem has a $3,000 limit for both knees, not a million.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: The insurance does not cover outpatient prescriptions, dental, allergy treatment or diabetic supplies. The membership that comes with it gives you discount programmes for those - you pay the discounted price yourself, nothing is reimbursed.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: The insurance excludes outpatient prescription drugs, dental services, speech therapy, allergy testing and injections, diabetic equipment supplies and self-management training, mental or nervous disorders, substance use disorders, autism spectrum disorder, and pregnancy except complications. The NCE non-insurance membership attached to the same product offers DISCOUNTS on prescriptions, dental, vision, speech therapy and diabetic supplies. Condition caps: $3,000 per coverage period for knee injury or disorder covering both knees combined, gallbladder surgery, appendectomy, kidney stones, TMJ and joint or tendon surgery; $50,000 transplants; $10,000 AIDS; ambulance $500 ground and $1,000 air per trip.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: Always separate the two lists out loud.

compliance_risks.do_not_say: For any product in this group, do not answer a coverage, exclusion, waiting-period or pre-existing question on a recorded call from portal material alone. Obtain the carrier document first.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: 51 of the 80 products on the NEO agent storefront have no brochure, certificate or policy document attached anywhere in the enrolment system. For those products the NEO reference page is the only available source, and four of those pages carry a limitations or exclusions heading with no text beneath it.

compliance_risks.do_not_say: Until the PDFs are filed, any compliance challenge to a benefit statement on these products can be answered only with the ledger's citations, not with the underlying document. Treat filing them as outstanding remediation, not housekeeping.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: Ten of the eleven linked brochures are READ and fully extracted into the ledger, but the PDF files themselves are not in Drive. The documents behind 25 live variants therefore exist in this project only as extracted facts, not as retrievable source documents.

carrier.v: THE BROCHURE NAMES TWO DIFFERENT CARRIERS. Cover block: 'Underwritten by American Financial SECURITY Life Insurance Co in AL, AR, AZ, KY, MS, NE, NV, OH, OK, TX, WI, GA, IL, IN, and VA.' Next sentence: 'This short-term medical insurance (evidenced by Certificate form AF ST CERT 818) is underwritten by American Financial SERVICES Life Insurance Company.' The Additional Plan Provisions section uses SERVICES: 'The Policy is underwritten by American Financial Services Life Insurance Company, 150 East Palmetto Parkway, Suite 450, Boca Raton, FL, 33432.'

network.v: The page labels the network 'First Health Network' but the provider-search URL it gives is www.MultiPlan.com/phcspracanc - a MultiPlan PHCS address.

product_type.v: 'Limited Duration Group Short Term Medical Insurance'. Certificate form AF ST CERT 818. Brochure code BR-AFS-STM-2022.

excluded_services.v: 61 numbered exclusions. Among those most likely to arise on a call: PREGNANCY AND RELATED SERVICES except Complications of Pregnancy; voluntary termination of pregnancy; OUTPATIENT PRESCRIPTION DRUGS, contraceptive drugs and devices, non-prescription drugs, vitamins, minerals and nutritional supplements; DENTAL SERVICES; MENTAL OR NERVOUS DISORDERS; SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS; SPEECH THERAPY; routine foot care; obesity, extreme obesity, morbid obesity or weight reduction including bariatric surgery and complications resulting from it; tobacco cessation; acne or varicose veins; sleeping disorders; ALLERGY TESTING AND ALLERGY INJECTIONS; DIABETIC EQUIPMENT, SUPPLIES AND SELF-MANAGEMENT TRAINING; AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER; learning disorders, disabilities or developmental delays; clinical trials; homeopathy; orthopedic manipulation; private duty nursing; acupuncture and acupressure; genetic testing or counselling; sex transformation and treatment of sexual function; growth hormones; eye examinations, eyeglasses, contact lenses and refractive surgery; CATARACTS; orthoptics; newborn dependants not yet discharged from hospital (except medically necessary treatment of premature birth, congenital injury or illness); cosmetic surgery; experimental or investigational treatment; care by a Close Relative; care the covered person is not legally required to pay for; pre-employment, pre-marital or routine physical examinations; work-related injury; war, riot or insurrection; felony or illegal occupation; hazardous activities including scuba diving, hang or ultralight gliding, ballooning, bungee jumping, parakiting, all-terrain vehicles, dirt bikes, snowmobiles and rodeo contests; and injury sustained while operating a motor vehicle above the legal impairment standard.

pre_existing.v: 36-MONTH LOOKBACK. The exclusion list defines a pre-existing condition as one 'for which medical advice, diagnosis, care, or treatment (includes receiving services and supplies, Consultations, diagnostic tests or prescription medicines) was recommended or received from a Physician within the 36 months immediately preceding the Covered Person's [effective date]'. The cover disclaimer states in capitals: 'PRE-EXISTING CONDITIONS ARE NOT COVERED, AND BENEFITS ARE SUBJECT TO THE POLICY LIMITATIONS AND EXCLUSIONS.'

waiting_period_other.v: 'Covered Persons will only receive Benefits for Illnesses that begin, by occurrence of symptoms and/or receipt of treatment, more than 5 days following the Covered Person's Effective Date.' Cancer: more than 30 days following the effective date. 'There is no waiting period for Injuries.'

addons.non_insurance.v: 'Non insurance association membership benefits are provided by The National Congress of Employers (NCE).' The membership bundles: dental discounts through a network whose dentists accept discounted contract rates as payment in full (discounts vary by geographical location); vision discounts; a prescription discount card saving an average of 15% on brand name and 55% on generic, accepted at over 80% of US pharmacies, usable by anyone in the family regardless of age, with no personal information collected; an INTERNATIONAL mail-order programme (MGI) saving up to 80% on brand-name medications; Patient Assistance Programs for those meeting income guidelines; chiropractic care; hearing; imaging; laboratory; nurse helpline; diabetic supplies savings; PET medication savings; CBD savings (broad spectrum, non-GMO, under 0.3% THC by weight); Speech Therapy through Great Speech Inc.; and MyTelemedicine, 'a non-emergency medical service with a nationwide group of licensed physicians who can diagnose, treat and provide prescriptions for non-narcotic/non-DEA/non-state-controlled substances'.

benefit.copays.v: Published per plan column. PLAN 1: Urgent Care copay $25, maximum 2; Specialist $40, maximum 2; Wellness $50, maximum 1. PLAN 2: Urgent Care $15, UNLIMITED; Specialist $25, UNLIMITED; Wellness $50, maximum 1; plus an Urgent Care Additional Deductible of $100 (maximum 1) and an Emergency Room Additional Deductible of $250 (maximum 1). PLAN 3: Urgent Care $25, maximum 2; Specialist $40, maximum 2; Wellness $50, maximum 1; no additional deductibles.

benefit.plan1_internal_limits.v: PLAN 1 ONLY carries hard dollar caps where Plans 2 and 3 are 'Subject to Deductible and Coinsurance': hospital room miscellaneous expense limited to $1,500; intensive/critical care miscellaneous medical charges limited to $2,000 per day; doctor visits during a hospital stay limited to $500 per covered person per coverage period; outpatient hospital surgery or ASC miscellaneous charges limited to $1,500 per day; outpatient miscellaneous hospital expenses limited to $1,500 per covered person per coverage period; emergency room treatment including professional and facility services not to exceed $250 per visit; surgeon $5,000 per surgery not to exceed $10,000 per coverage period; assistant surgeon $1,000 per surgery not to exceed $2,000; anaesthesia $1,000 per surgery not to exceed $2,000.

benefit.shared_limits.v: Identical across all three plan columns, subject to deductible and coinsurance: organ/tissue/bone marrow transplants up to $50,000 per coverage period; extended care facility $100/day, 30 days; hospice $5,000; AIDS $10,000; joint/tendon surgery $3,000; knee injury or disorder $3,000 for BOTH knees combined; gallbladder surgery $3,000; appendectomy $3,000; kidney stones $3,000; TMJ $3,000; home health care $30/day, maximum 30 days; physical, speech and occupational therapy $30/day, maximum 15 days; ambulance $500 ground / $1,000 air per trip; durable medical equipment subject to deductible and coinsurance.

benefit.structure.v: Deductible options $500, $1,000, $2,000, $2,500, $5,000, $7,500, $10,000. Coinsurance 80%/20%. Coinsurance limit $2,000 or $4,000. Coverage Period Maximum options $250,000, $500,000, $1,000,000. Length of coverage: 'Available for up to 36 months of coverage depending upon state regulations.'

compliance.aca_disclaimer.v: Cover disclaimer, printed in capitals: 'THIS COVERAGE IS NOT REQUIRED TO COMPLY WITH CERTAIN FEDERAL MARKET REQUIREMENTS FOR HEALTH INSURANCE, PRINCIPALLY THOSE CONTAINED IN THE AFFORDABLE CARE ACT... YOUR COVERAGE ALSO HAS LIFETIME AND/OR COVERAGE PERIOD DOLLAR LIMITS ON HEALTH BENEFITS. IF THIS COVERAGE EXPIRES OR YOU LOSE ELIGIBILITY FOR THIS COVERAGE, YOU MIGHT HAVE TO WAIT UNTIL AN OPEN ENROLLMENT PERIOD TO GET OTHER HEALTH INSURANCE COVERAGE.' Coverage Provisions: 'the insurance coverage is not minimum essential benefits as set forth under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act.'

consecutive_terms.v: 'When a member applies for consecutive terms in one enrollment, they will be issued their initial term of coverage, and subsequent terms will be pending. The waiting period on all subsequent terms will be waived. Members will not have to reapply for additional terms. When subsequent terms of coverage are set to begin, the member will receive an email stating their plan has continued into the next term. The email will provide them with their new monthly rate (if applicable), and they will have the opportunity to opt out at that time.' 'Deductible and coinsurance and all benefit limits will RESET with each 12 month period of coverage.'

eligibility.v: Cover block: 'Eligibility 18 - 64 1/2. Child coverage policies from 2-17.' Additional Plan Provisions: 'plans are made available to members of NCE, and their spouses, and dependent children between the ages of 6 MONTHS and 64 and 11 months of age WHO CAN ANSWER "NO" TO ALL THE QUESTIONS IN THE ENROLLMENT APPLICATION FOR INSURANCE. Association membership is not required in all states.'

exclusions.weekend_admission.v: Exclusion 10: 'Inpatient Hospital admission occurring on a Friday or Saturday in conjunction with a surgical procedure scheduled to be performed during the following week. A Sunday admission will be eligible only for the procedure scheduled to be performed early Monday morning. (This limitation will not apply to necessary medical admissions requiring immediate attention or to Emergency surgical admissions).'

premium_changes.v: 'We have the right to change the premium We charge. We will send You a notice at least 31 days before We make any premium rate change.'

riders.pre_existing_waiver.v: 'Pre-Existing Waiver Rider option will waive any conditions that were covered during the prior coverage period which means consumers will not have to re-qualify for another term to begin. Terms of coverage and limitations may vary by state.' Also: 'If the member has selected the pre-ex waiver rider, the waiting periods for sickness and cancer will be waived in subsequent terms.'

source_content.info_panel.v: The INFORMATION panel is 112 characters and contains ONE line: 'First Health Network - Provider Search: www.MultiPlan.com/phcspracanc'. No benefit schedule, no deductible, no coinsurance, no maximum, no term length, no exclusions, no waiting periods, no pre-existing provision. The TERMS panel renders zero characters.

termination.v: Coverage terminates on the earliest of: the last day premium was paid; entering armed forces active duty exceeding 31 days; termination of the Policy; 'THE DATE YOU REACH AGE 65 OR BECOME EFFECTIVE UNDER MEDICARE'; ceasing to be a Member of the Policyholder; the end of the Coverage Period; death; reaching the Coverage Period Maximum Benefit Amount; the effective date in the event of fraud in obtaining coverage; or the next premium due date in the event of fraud in filing a claim.
